title: SELF DRIVE Act of 2026
summary: The bill would require automated-driving-system manufacturers to prepare evidence-backed safety cases for each system version, with a federal rule due by September 2027. It would also create a national crash data repository, requiring qualifying crash reports within 30 days or 10 days after notice and quarterly reports of automated-driving miles.

title: AV Safety Data Act
summary: This introduced bill, not enacted law, would direct the head of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to issue rules within 90 days requiring manufacturers and operators already covered by its 2025 incident-reporting order to file monthly reports on miles driven, injury-causing collisions, and "unplanned stoppage" events involving automated or Level 2 driver-assistance vehicles. The agency would publish the data online within 120 days and could not weaken the rules for 10 years.

title: AV Emergency Response Coordination Act
summary: This introduced bill would require operators and makers of vehicles with automated driving systems to maintain an emergency hotline, available at all times and answered within 30 seconds, beginning 90 days after enactment. Under proposed section 2(f), the hotline would let emergency responders coordinate with the company and its remote human personnel during emergencies.

title: Autonomous Vehicle Acceleration Act of 2025
summary: Section 4 would require the Secretary of Transportation, acting through the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, to address within one year of enactment the certification barriers identified in a 2016 Volpe Center report, including presumptions of a human driver. The Secretary could update, interpret, or exempt federal motor vehicle safety standards for Level 4 and Level 5 autonomous vehicles, and would report to Congress 180 days after that deadline.

title: AMERICA DRIVES Act
summary: This introduced bill would add a new section to federal transportation law stating that commercial trucks with Level 4 or Level 5 automated driving systems (ADS, self-driving technology) could operate in interstate commerce with no human driver on board and no remote human driver. It would direct the Secretary of Transportation to issue implementing regulations. It would also not require any vehicle to have ADS.

title: Shared Autonomous Mobility Act of 2026
summary: This introduced bill would require the Secretary of Transportation to create, within 90 days of enactment, a competitive grant program for deploying new automated-driving buses, with at least 15 percent of funds reserved for rural projects, an 80 percent federal cost share cap, and $100 million authorized across fiscal years 2027–2028. It would also direct a dedicated test facility by January 1, 2027.
